transcript:
Meeting header:
- Date: 2026-11-12
- Start: 16:00 UTC
- Duration: ~47 minutes
- Attendees: Samir Patel (Redwood AE), Kara Nguyen (Redwood SE), Luis Romero (Redwood SE), Ellen Mora (Argospring CTO), Diego Ruiz (Head of Cloud), Priya Iyer (VP Partnerships), Marcus Chen (SRE)

Auto-summary (auto-gen, may be rough):
Argospring is evaluating Redwood for a hybrid onramp: keep some sensitive inference in their VPC while routing bursty traffic to hosted capacity. They care about predictable latency (<=120ms p95 for short NLU queries), unit cost per token, and integration complexity with their KMS and SSO. They asked about fallback behavior when Dedicated pool is saturated and about prefix caching / kv cache for conversational state. Redwood AE/SE outlined Dedicated vs Hosted vs Private tradeoffs and suggested a 1-week benchmark with representative prompt set.

Topics covered:
- Hybrid onramp architecture and routing policies
- Capacity sizing and reserved vs burst options
- KV cache / prefix caching and batching recommendations
- Security requirements: KMS, SSO, SOC2, audit logs
- Pilot scope and next steps

Transcript body:
[00:00] Samir: Hey everyone, thanks for carving out time, I'm Samir with Redwood, AE on the account. Quick roll call?
[00:06] Ellen: Hi Samir, Ellen here, CTO at Argospring.
[00:09] Diego: Diego Ruiz, head of cloud infra.
[00:11] Priya: Priya, partnerships - I'll be shepherding this from a commercial side.
[00:14] Marcus: Marcus Chen, SRE.
[00:16] Kara: Kara Nguyen, SE at Redwood. Luis is with me as well.
[00:20] Luis: Hey all.
[00:22] Samir: Cool. Two goals today: orient on your current stack + constraints, and then walk through a proposed hybrid onramp pilot that balances cost and latency. Is that OK?
[00:30] Ellen: Yep that's perfect. We're evaluating vendors for a hybrid strategy — some inference stays on our VPC/onprem, and the rest goes to a managed endpoint. Main things: p95 latency SLAs and predictable monthly GPU spend.
[00:44] Samir: Got it. Diego, can you quickly sketch current infra? What models are you running and what traffic shape?
[00:51] Diego: Sure. We run a mix — most of our production is smaller NLU models, custom fine-tuned 7B-ish models for intent detection and entity extraction. Peaks are pretty spiky, like heavy bursts around campaign times. Baseline QPS is small, maybe a couple hundred requests per minute, but spiky bursts go to thousands.
[01:12] Kara: When you say "7B-ish", are these off-the-shelf LMs or heavier fine-tuned weights? Any KV cache usage today?
[01:20] Diego: Fine-tuned. We don't have a KV cache today, it's pretty stateless per request, except we keep a short convo history in the client.
[01:27] Luis: That actually matters a lot for batching and cost. If it's stateless you get better batching but less benefit from prefix cache.
[01:33] Marcus: For us the requirement is p95 under 120ms for small NLU prompts. Anything above that, product folks will complain.
[01:39] Samir: Right. So two levers: dedicated/reserved capacity for steady-state latency guarantees and a hosted burst/backfill for spiky demand. With Redwood Dedicated you can get predictable tail latencies because you reserve GPU pools and set autoscale policies. If you tie that with prefix KV caching and smaller quantized model variants, the per-token cost drops and latency improves.
[01:59] Ellen: Can you clarify "prefix KV cache"? I've seen references in your doc but not sure how it maps to our convo-state.
[02:07] Kara: Sure. Roughly, KV cache stores the transformer key/value states so you don't recompute the full prefix on every generation. For conversational flows with long prefixes it saves a lot of compute. But if your current client already sends short per-request context then the win is smaller. Also, KV cache is most effective when you keep the same model instance warm — which Dedicated helps with.
[02:34] Diego: How does that interact with private deployments? If we put Redwood Private in our VPC, do we still get the cache and kernel optimizations?
[02:43] Luis: Yes. The runtime is the same across modes — we ship the same inference engine. Kernel selection, quantization paths, all of that is available in Private. The main diffs are control plane location, where data lives, and operational tie-ins like your KMS.
[02:58] Priya: From the partnership perspective, we need to know the minimum commitment and the burst overage pricing. Also, what happens if the Dedicated pool is saturated? Does traffic queue, drop, or automatically route to hosted endpoints?
[03:12] Samir: Good question. You can set routing rules. Typical pattern: primary route to Dedicated (for latency-sensitive traffic), fallback to hosted variants or a cheaper quantized model variant in another region. Redwood can do automated fallback — you set policies for cost vs latency tradeoffs. If you prefer, traffic can queue briefly or we can failover to your Private nodes if available.
[03:33] Ellen: Any example SLOs customers get with a 2-GPU per-region dedicated pool? Ballpark numbers?
[03:39] Kara: For small 7B-ish models with int8 quant, typical p95 is 50-120ms depending on sequence length. We usually benchmark with sequence length of 64 tokens for NLU. We'll put together a small matrix for you.
[03:52] Diego: We need that matrix: p50/p95, cost per 1k tokens, and also what happens to tail when you get cold starts.
[03:59] Luis: We'll include cold-start profiles and warmup strategies. Note — continuous batching + smart routing reduces cold starts by keeping warm instances and reusing batch slots. But if you scale to zero aggressively, you'll see more variability.
[04:14] Marcus: Security — we need KMS integration (customer-managed keys), SSO via SAML, SOC2 compliance, and audit logs for inference payloads. Also, data residency in EU for certain customers.
[04:25] Samir: All of those are supported. Private deployment gives you KMS/HSM integration and keeps logs inside your control plane. For hosted, we support customer-managed encryption keys via cloud KMS integrations and retention policies. We can share SOC2 docs after this call.
[04:40] Ellen: What about PII scrubbing or data redaction? Some of our prompts include user identifiers. Can you do token-level redaction?
[04:48] Kara: We offer middleware hooks in the router so you can pre-process requests for redaction. We also have the option to not persist payloads for hosted flows and to disable logging for specific routes. We'll include practices in the security pack.
[05:02] Priya: Commercially, we're looking at a 3-month pilot to validate latency and cost. If that looks good, a Q1 2027 reserved capacity commit. What should a pilot look like?
[05:12] Samir: Typical pilot is 2-4 weeks, but for routing-balance and latency you get better signal with 1-week live traffic plus synthetic load tests. Proposed pilot: provision a small Dedicated pool in one region, configure routing rules for a portion of traffic, run synthetic bursts, and collect p95/p99 and cost per token metrics. We can also run a private-deploy smoke test if you want.
[05:36] Diego: Can we bring our own model? We want to bring our fine-tuned 7B weights. Any constraints on model formats?
[05:43] Luis: We take standard checkpoints — PyTorch/pt or ONNX artifacts. For best perf we recommend a quantized model or we can run quantization as part of onboarding. There are some model-architecture caveats but we'll run a compatibility check.
[05:57] Marcus: Network: we need VPC peering and TTL for connections, do you support private peering and fixed egress IPs?
[06:05] Kara: Yes, Private supports VPC peering and private endpoints. Hosted can support egress IP ranges for allowlisting and we offer a VPC onramp for hybrid setups. We'll capture the exact requirements in the network diagram.
[06:18] Ellen: Another question — how do you handle model rollouts and canaries? We want canary traffic split and automatic fallback to previous model on regressions.
[06:26] Samir: Redwood Console supports rollouts, A/B splits, canary percentage, and automated quality regressions if you tie it to eval sets. You can configure automatic rollback policies based on latency or model score thresholds.
[06:37] Priya: Competitors popped into our procurement team — HashServe and LoomCloud. How do you position Redwood vs those?
[06:44] Samir: Short answer: Redwood is focused on production economics and unified runtime across hosted/dedicated/private. Many competitors are either pure hosted API or focused purely on on-prem runtimes with less orchestration. We'll send a one-pager comparison.
[06:57] Diego: Can you do a quick sketch of the pilot timeline and deliverables?
[07:02] Samir: Sure:
- Week 0: onboarding + model check (we run compatibility and quantization test)
- Week 1: deploy Dedicated pool + route ~10% of traffic, start synthetic burst tests
- Week 2: ramp to 25-50%, collect latency/cost metrics and analyze KV cache effectiveness
- Week 3: finalize pilot report and recommendation for reserved commitments or Private deployment
[07:26] Marcus: Sounds ok. For the model check we will need to share a sample weights tar and prompt set.
[07:31] Kara: Perfect. Also we'll send a small checklist for infra pre-reqs (VPC peering, allowed ports, KMS IAM roles).
[07:40] Ellen: What's the typical turnaround to get us a Dedicated pool provisioned?
[07:44] Samir: For standard regions it's 3-5 business days once contracts and billing are in place; in constrained regions it can be longer. For a pilot we can often use shared hosted capacity with priority routing same day if you want to validate routing policies faster.
[07:58] Diego: One more thing — tail cost. How do we get predictability? We hate surprise egress or token billing.
[08:05] Samir: We offer committed monthly spend options for Dedicated and caps for hosted usage. Also detailed token-level billing per route in the Console so you can segment spend. We'll highlight controls like throttles, per-route quotas, and pre-warming to limit surprises.
[08:20] Luis: On the technical note, if Argospring wants to keep strict p95, you'd probably reserve enough Dedicated to cover baseline QPS plus a buffer for typical bursts, then route overflow to hosted model variants. Caching will buy you more headroom in Dedicated.
[08:33] Marcus: Ok. For SSO we use Okta and SAML, can you integrate?
[08:38] Kara: Yes Okta SAML is supported. We'll need a metadata XML and an SP configuration on your side. We'll attach steps in the onboarding doc.
[08:48] Priya: From a partnership standpoint, is there co-marketing if we proceed? We might run a case study if the pilot yields good ROI.
[08:55] Samir: Absolutely. We typically do a joint case study after a successful pilot. We'll align legal and PR later.
[09:03] Ellen: Anything else on the security checklist?
[09:06] Luis: We'll provide SOC2 and network diagrams. For payload retention we can configure per-route retention and a "no-persist" flag. Also, if you want end-to-end encryption, Private with your KMS is the way to go.
[09:20] Diego: Ok let's talk deliverables.
[09:22] Samir: Action items recap: Samir sends pricing and quickstart deck; Kara drafts benchmark plan; Marcus shares network diagram; customer shares model artifact + prompt set. We'll aim to start the pilot the week of 2026-11-22 if we get artifacts in time.
[09:38] Priya: That timeline would work for us.
[09:42] Ellen: Thanks everyone. If you can also include a short cost model showing Dedicated vs hosted for our traffic patterns that would help procurement.
[09:51] Samir: Will do. Kara, any final technical notes?
[09:54] Kara: Just that the benchmark matrix will include p50/p95/p99, token cost, KV cache delta, and cold-start overhead. We'll draft and share.
[10:03] Diego: Great. Thanks.
[10:05] Samir: Thanks all, we'll follow up with the docs and schedule the benchmark kickoff.

End of call.
